text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS

-- Vietnamese and Malaysian parliamentary leaders yesterday expressed their desire for stronger links, saying closer ties would benefit both nations' economic development. The statement was made during talks in Kuala Lumpur between Nong Duc Manh, Chairman of Vietnam's National Assembly, and Mohamed Zahia, Speaker of the Malaysian House of Representatives.

-- A tropical low was moving towards the Tonkin Gulf early yesterday afternoon at a speed of 20 km (12.5 miles) per hour. The depression, with winds of about 60 km (37.5 miles) per hour, was expected to have hit Vietnam's central coast very early this morning.

-- The Asian Development Bank has approved a further grant of $1.3 million in technical assistance for upgrading Vietnam's major national Highway 1. Part of the grant is to be used to improve a stretch of the road between the Nha Trang coastal resort and the central province of Quang Ngai province.

-- The second annual international workshop on oil and gas development in continental southeast Asia is running from Tuesday to Friday. The workshop focuses on regulations and policies for the prevention of polution in the industry.
-- Motorola demonstrated several models of two-way radio, aimed primarily at law enforcement and security applications, in Ho Chi Minh City.

-- Samsung Vina Electronics, the first Vietnam-South Korea electronics joint venture, will hold an inauguration ceremony for its factory in Ho Chi Minh City today. The $36.5 million venture has already conducted three months of trial production. - - - -
LE COURRIER DU VIETNAM

-- The director of the World Bank's Asia-Pacific department promised at a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai to support Vietnam in settling its debts with the London Club of commercial creditors.
-- The meteoroligcal departments of Vietnam and Thailand had talks about cooperation on technology and equipment in the coming years. - - - -
NHAN DAN
-- Over 400 hamlets and wards in Dong Nai province joined a campaign to build new life and eliminate poverty and hunger.
-- Quang Nam-Da Nang's Communist Party Committee said more efforts wrere needed to fight against corruption and smuggling.
-- A delegation from the External Affairs Department of the Communist Party's Central Committee conducted a two-day official visit to China. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN
-- A two-day conference on the State's Decree on Militia Forces was held in Hanoi by the Ministry of Defence.
HA NOI MOI

-- The Ministry of Construction unveiled a detailed masterplan for the area around central Hanoi's Hoan Kiem lake, which gives priorities to municipal offices, banks, a trade centre, hotels and public cultural places.
-- Hanoi's police force is preparing a new campaign to implement the government's decreen on rail and water transport safety.
-- The Hanoi People's Council said the campaign against social evils was making good progress, but expressed concern over the increasing number of teenage drug users.
